config.title: Design Notification System

intro.title: Design Notification System
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple notification system that displays messages to users, such as alerts or updates. You will learn how to manage dynamic content in Vue by using reactive state to store and update notifications. The main technologies involved are Vue's reactive data properties, conditional rendering with v-if, and event handling with methods. By the end, you'll have a functional component that can show and hide notifications based on user interactions.
intro.usecase: Notification systems are essential in modern web applications to keep users informed about important events. You'll see them in e-commerce platforms showing order confirmations, social media apps displaying new messages, and productivity tools alerting about task deadlines. As a Vue developer, you'll implement these notifications in dashboards, admin panels, and user interfaces where real-time feedback is crucial. This pattern helps create professional, user-friendly applications that communicate effectively with users.

objectives: Construct a reactive notification state using Vue's ref or reactive API
Implement a notification component that renders messages with different types (success, error, warning)
Configure a notification system to automatically remove messages after a specified duration
Integrate a notification service with application components using provide/inject or composables
Manipulate the notification queue to add, remove, and clear messages programmatically
Apply conditional rendering to display notifications based on user interactions or API responses
Bind notification visibility to user actions like close buttons or automatic timeouts
Control notification positioning and styling using Vue's class and style bindings

steps.title: Import Vue and ref from 'vue'
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the ref function from the 'vue' package to set up your component and reactive state.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and ref from the 'vue' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing Vue and a reactive function
import { ref } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have access to Vue's core functionality and the ref function for creating reactive state.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both Vue and ref from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.

steps.title: Create the NotificationSystem component
steps.instruction: Define and export a default Vue component named NotificationSystem that returns a template with a single root element.
steps.hint: Create a component function that returns a template. In Vue, components must have a single root element in their template.
steps.expectedOutcome: A NotificationSystem component is created and exported as the default export.
successCriteria: The NotificationSystem component is defined and exported as default with a template containing a single root element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the component, but make sure it's exported as default and has a template with a single root element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't properly defined. Check that you're exporting a default Vue component named NotificationSystem with a template.

steps.title: Initialize notifications array state with ref
steps.instruction: Inside the NotificationSystem component, use ref to create a reactive notifications array with an initial empty array value.
steps.hint: Declare a const variable named notifications and assign it the result of calling ref([]).
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: reactive array state
const items = ref([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a reactive notifications array ready to store notification objects.
successCriteria: A notifications variable is declared using ref with an initial empty array value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using ref with an empty array [] as the initial value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The notifications array state wasn't initialized correctly. Try using ref([]) to create reactive state.

steps.title: Define addNotification handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, define a function named addNotification that takes two parameters: message and type. This function should push a new notification object (with id, message, and type properties) to the notifications array.
steps.hint: Create a function that receives message and type, then uses notifications.value.push() to add an object with those properties plus a unique id (you can use Date.now() for simplicity).
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have an addNotification function ready to be used for adding notifications to the state.
successCriteria: The addNotification function is defined inside setup, takes message and type parameters, and pushes a notification object to notifications.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function takes both message and type parameters and pushes an object with id, message, and type to notifications.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The addNotification function isn't defined correctly. Check that it's inside setup, takes two parameters, and pushes to notifications.value.

steps.title: Define removeNotification handler function
steps.instruction: Define a function named removeNotification that takes an id parameter and filters out the notification with that id from the notifications array.
steps.hint: Inside the setup function, create a function that receives an id and updates notifications.value to only keep items whose id doesn't match.
steps.expectedOutcome: The removeNotification function is defined and ready to be used to remove notifications by their id.
successCriteria: A removeNotification function is defined that takes an id parameter and filters notifications.value to exclude the notification with that id.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function takes an id parameter and properly filters the notifications array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The removeNotification function isn't defined correctly. It should take an id parameter and filter notifications.value to remove the matching notification.

steps.title: Add main container div to template
steps.instruction: In the component's return statement, add a div element with the class 'notification-system' as the root template element.
steps.hint: The return statement should return an object with a template property containing the div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a root div element with the class 'notification-system' in its template.
successCriteria: The component's return statement includes a template property with a div element having class 'notification-system'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning an object with a template property containing the div element with the correct class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The return statement doesn't yet contain the required div element with class 'notification-system'.

steps.title: Add notification display section
steps.instruction: Inside the main container div, add a new div element with the class 'notifications-container' to serve as the area where notifications will be displayed.
steps.hint: This div will act as a wrapper for the notification items you'll add later. Make sure it's placed inside the existing main container.
steps.analogousExample: // Adding a container for items
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now includes a notifications-container div inside the main notification-system container, ready to hold notification items.
successCriteria: A div with class 'notifications-container' is added inside the main container div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the div has the exact class 'notifications-container' and is placed inside the main container.
steps.feedbackWrong: The notifications display section wasn't added correctly. Check that you've added a div with class 'notifications-container' inside the main container.

steps.title: Render notifications using v-for
steps.instruction: Inside the notifications-container div, use v-for to iterate through the notifications array and render each notification in a div element.
steps.hint: Use v-for to loop through notifications and display each item's content.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: rendering list items
  • {{ item.name }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The notifications array will be iterated in the template, ready to display each notification.
successCriteria: A v-for directive is used to iterate through notifications, and each notification is rendered in a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using v-for correctly to iterate through the notifications array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The notifications are not being rendered. Check that you're using v-for to loop through the notifications array.

steps.title: Add close button to each notification
steps.instruction: Inside the v-for loop, add a button element with a click handler that calls removeNotification, passing the current notification's id.
steps.hint: Add a button inside the notification div. Use @click to call removeNotification with notification.id.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler in Vue
<button @click="removeItem(item.id)">Close</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: Each notification will have a close button that, when clicked, removes that specific notification from the list.
successCriteria: A button element is added inside the v-for loop with @click="removeNotification(notification.id)".
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it's inside the v-for loop and calls removeNotification with the notification's id.
steps.feedbackWrong: The close button is missing or not properly configured. Add a button with @click="removeNotification(notification.id)" inside the notification div.

steps.title: Add notification controls section
steps.instruction: Add a div with class 'controls' inside the notification-system container, containing buttons that call addNotification with different message and type values when clicked.
steps.hint: Create a div with class='controls' and add multiple button elements inside it. Each button should have an @click handler that calls addNotification with a specific message and type.
steps.analogousExample: // Adding a controls section with buttons
steps.expectedOutcome: The notification system will have a controls section with buttons that allow adding different types of notifications when clicked.
successCriteria: A div with class 'controls' is added inside the notification-system container, containing at least two buttons with @click handlers that call addNotification with different message and type values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some controls, but make sure you have a div with class='controls' containing multiple buttons that call addNotification with different parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The controls section is missing or incomplete. Add a div with class='controls' containing buttons that call addNotification when clicked.
